subject: Borealis: production inference surge — recovery playbook & exec readout
messages:
From: Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@borealis.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: amit.rao@borealis.com, sre@borealis.com
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: High latency + 5xx spike impacting Checkout (prod)

Hi Rishi —

We started seeing a sustained latency increase and elevated 5xx rates on inference endpoints backing our Checkout funnel around 08:50 PST. Conversion dropped ~12% in 25 minutes. Our SRE team attached sample traces and metrics (borealis-telemetry-snapshot-20261125.zip).

Can Redwood confirm:
- Whether there were any model pushes or config changes on your end between 08:30–09:00 PST
- Any capacity or routing events in us-west-2 that could explain a sudden throughput contraction

We need a bridge, and our execs want a quick recovery plan and an ETA for root cause analysis.

Thanks,
Emma
VP Product, Borealis

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@borealis.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: High latency + 5xx spike impacting Checkout (prod)

Emma —

Acknowledged. Thanks for the telemetry — that helps a lot. We're standing up an incident bridge now. Initial notes: no model pushes scheduled from our side in the window, but we are seeing elevated queueing in a small subset of host pools (us-west-2, pool-id p-7Gf).

Immediate plan (next 90 mins):
- Bridge (RDW-Borealis-Bridge) — owners: Ben (runtime), Laura (customer comms), Grace (SRE liaison)
- Failover routing to warm pools in us-east-1 for priority Checkout traffic (non-disruptive subset)
- Temporary throttling of non-critical background calls (to conserve tokens)

I'll post bridge dial and runbook link in 5m.

—Rishi
Director, Priority Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:47:00 -0800
Subject: RDW-Borealis-Bridge: initial findings

Bridge notes (summary):
- 09:05–09:20: Query queue depth for p-7Gf rose ~6x due to a backfill job that coincided with a checkout traffic spike from Borealis. Backfill was started by an internal data-sync job.
- Two GPUs in p-7Gf experienced elevated kernel preemption causing token latency to climb; kernel-level retries bubbled up as 5xxs for ~12 minutes.
- We executed a targeted evict-and-warm for Borealis' routes at 09:28 and shifted ~35% of Checkout traffic to us-east-1 warm pools; tail latency returned to baseline by 09:38.

Actions completed:
- Evict offending backfill job (owner: infra-data) — blocked further queue pressure
- Applied route override and traffic split
- Saved telemetry snapshot and uploaded to shared drive

Immediate ask for Borealis: can your team share whether any checkout-side batch jobs aligned at 08:45? It will help us correlate root cause.

Attachment: borealis-telemetry-snapshot-20261125.zip (uploaded)

—Ben
Senior SRE, Redwood

We confirmed a data-sync window overlapped Checkout at 08:42–09:05; that explains a lot. We're also seeing a spike in retries client-side during the 5xx window.

Please add the following to the RCA scope:

—Amit
SRE Lead, Borealis

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@borealis.com>, Amit Rao <amit.rao@borealis.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: RCA draft + corrective playbook (attached)

Team —

Attached is a draft RCA and a short corrective playbook (rishi_borealis-rca-draft-v1.docx, post-incident-playbook.pdf). Highlights:

Root cause summary (short):
- A scheduled internal data-sync backfill overlapped a Checkout traffic peak. Backfill increased queue depth in host pool p-7Gf.
- Two GPUs showed kernel preemption events under sustained queue pressure; this surfaced as transient 5xx responses.
- Lack of cross-team throttling between batch/backfill and low-latency inference traffic allowed contention to propagate to priority routes.

Corrective actions (owner / ETA):
1) Immediate: Harden routing rules to prevent backfill jobs from scheduling into hot inference host pools (owner: infra-data / ETA: 48h).
2) Short term: Add a pre-evict health probe that detects kernel preemption signals and proactively drains affected hosts (owner: runtime / ETA: 72h).
3) Mid term: Cross-team scheduling policy (batch vs latency-sensitive) and a quota guardrail enforced at cluster-scheduler level (owner: infra-platform / ETA: 3 weeks).
4) Customer-visible: Enhanced incident playbook and an SLA credit proposal template for impact windows >10m (owner: account team / ETA: 5 business days).

Deliverables we've attached/linked:
- Detailed telemetry and trace correlation (Drive link)
- Draft slide for Borealis exec readout (for your review)
- A compact remediation checklist we can run during future surges

Requests from Borealis:
- Confirmation that the slide and the short playbook cover the level of detail your CTO needs for an exec readout
- Approval to open a joint Jira (INF-8221) for the cross-team scheduling policy work

I'll run a 30-minute exec sync with you on Monday; please confirm availability.

Best,
Rishi
